chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would face the people and say: 'O assembly of Muslims, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan appears, the rebels of the devils are shackled, the gates of heaven are opened, the gates of mercy are opened, and the gates of hellfire are closed, and supplication is answered. And for Allah, at every breaking of the fast (Eid), there are slaves freed from the hellfire. A caller proclaims every night: 'Is there any supplicant? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a substitute, and give every hoarder a loss.' Until the crescent of Shawal appears, it is proclaimed to the believers: 'Go forth to your rewards,' for it is the Day of Reward.'
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are not the reward of dinars and dirhams (coins/money).'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and events that occur during the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical shifts in Ramadan, noting the restraint of rebellious devils and the unlocking of divine mercy, which culminates in the liberation of souls from Hellfire upon Eid al-Fitr. The Imam clarifies that the 'rewards' (jawazib) announced by the caller are not material gold or silver, but rather spiritual emancipation and divine grace, underscoring the eschatological significance of the month's worship.
